card.name: Study population after study or dose
card.fires_on: Small words like "in" or "to" right after a study, dose or exposure phrase, just before the group of people studied (healthy subjects, patients, women). Seen in clinical pharmacology and drug interaction sections.

modes.label: in after a study
modes.description: The word "in" follows a named study type and introduces the participants.
modes.example: An open-label, randomized, three-way crossover study<< in>> 18 healthy subjects assessed the effect

modes.label: to after given
modes.description: The word "to" follows given or coadministered and leads into the recipients.
modes.example: When nefazodone (200 mg BID) was given<< to>> patients being treated with theophylline

modes.label: in after a measure
modes.description: The word "in" follows a drug exposure measure such as AUC or a steady-state level, before the group it was measured in.
modes.example: approximately 2 and 0.5 times, respectively, the AUC<< in>> patients receiving the recommended dose

card.writes: It promotes words about evaluating and assessing, which suggests the text goes on to describe an evaluation of the group.
card.plain: It marks the little word that introduces who took part in a drug study.
